reported.title: Limit switch polarity inverted, so motor enable follows the opposite of the switch
reported.description: The limit is active LOW (pressed pulls D2 to GND), but limitActiveRaw() at line 20 returns true when digitalRead(LIMIT_PIN) == HIGH, and line 69 computes hit = (stableLimit == HIGH), so the firmware treats a released switch as a hit. Consequently line 74 disables the motor while the limit is clear and lines 76-82 enable it while the limit is active, inverting the required D13 behaviour. The measured evidence shows D13 not HIGH for 700 ms while required at t=100 ms and not LOW for 48 ms at t=901.5 ms, matching the inverted mapping. D13 was in the wrong state for 4842 ms across 31 interval(s), first at 100 ms: D13 was not HIGH for 700 ms while required (grace 100 ms).

truth.description: Treats pull-up HIGH as active limit

truth_for_judge.description: Treats pull-up HIGH as active limit

exposing_checks.behaviour: D13 must follow its stimulus; HIGH when D2 == 1; LOW when D2 == 0; within 100 ms (Motor off while limit LOW)

judge_input.spec:
- Limit switch on D2 with INPUT_PULLUP (pressed/active = LOW). Motor enable on D13. Jog on D4 (pull-up).
- Motor enable on D13 must be LOW (disabled) while the limit is active (D2 LOW), and HIGH otherwise.
- Reach the commanded motor state within 100 ms of a settled limit change.
- Debounce the limit contact with at least 25 ms of stability before acting.
- Print `rail motor=<0|1> hits=<n>` every 900 ms.
- Jog may request motion only when the limit is clear; limit always wins.
